s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive cerebellopontine angle syndrome with headache and neurologic deficits
salient_findings: Large lobulated mass at the left cerebellopontine angle
key_facts: 33-year-old man with no significant past medical history
3-month history of progressively worsening occipital headache
Headache exacerbated by Valsalva maneuvers
Bilateral past-pointing and intention tremor on neurologic examination
6.9 × 5.5 × 6.1 cm lobulated mass centered at the left cerebellopontine angle
Mass extended craniocaudally from the left ambient cistern to the premedullary space
Involvement and expansion of Meckel’s cave
Small extension into the left infratemporal fossa via the foramen ovale
Multiloculated T1-hypointense, T2-FLAIR–partially suppressible nonenhancing cystic areas
Interspersed enhancing septa and T1/T2-isointense enhancing solid components
Curvilinear signal loss with corresponding T1 hyperintensity consistent with hemorrhagic foci
Compression of the left cerebellum and brainstem
Dilation of the third, fourth, and lateral ventricles
Anterior displacement of the cavernous sinus
Encasement with mild narrowing of the left petrous internal carotid artery

shortlist.label: Trigeminal schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Mass location at cerebellopontine angle and involvement of Meckel's cave

shortlist.label: Schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Multiloculated cystic areas and enhancing septa, consistent with schwannoma characteristics

shortlist.label: Meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: Dural tail sign not mentioned, but location and mass effect suggest possibility

shortlist.label: Chordoma
shortlist.why_kept: Location at cerebellopontine angle and clivus erosion, although less common

shortlist.label: Cystic schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic components with enhancing septa, consistent with cystic schwannoma features

raw.rationale: The tumor's location at the left cerebellopontine angle, involvement and expansion of Meckel’s cave, and extension into the left infratemporal fossa via the foramen ovale are consistent with a trigeminal schwannoma. The presence of multiloculated cystic areas and enhancing septa also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Schwannoma
rejected.why: Too general, as the specific type of schwannoma is likely trigeminal schwannoma given the location and characteristics

rejected.label: Meningioma
rejected.why: Excluded due to the absence of typical meningioma features such as a dural tail and the presence of cystic areas

rejected.label: Chordoma
rejected.why: Unlikely due to the lack of midline involvement and the presence of cystic areas with enhancing septa

rejected.label: Cystic schwannoma
rejected.why: While the tumor has cystic components, the specific diagnosis of trigeminal schwannoma is more accurate given the location and other characteristics
